mappings.note: sec t - tan t = m to sec t + tan t: the work is factorising sec^2 - tan^2 = 1 and inverting, i.e. applying a derived identity to an algebraic relation, not stating or deriving the identity itself (LO-1)
pure substitution of sin 30 and cos 30 into 2 sin t cos t; no identity is used and no triangle is built, so the standard-angle table alone answers it

asks which of four identity STATEMENTS is false (tan^2 - sec^2 = 1 vs cosec^2 - cot^2 = 1); the demand is knowing how the two derived Pythagorean identities are oriented, which is LO-1, not applying one to simplify (LO-2)
simplifies cot^2 - cosec^2 to -1 by substituting cosec^2 = 1 + cot^2; an expression is reduced, so LO-2 rather than the statement-level LO-1

figure question: sin 30 = BC/AC with AC known, so a standard-angle value is used to produce a side. Deliberately NOT C-6.3 - no line of sight, no elevation angle, it is a bare right triangle

reads angles back OUT of the table (sin a = root3/2 gives 60, cos b = 0 gives 90); the 0/90 end of the standard-angle row is the whole content

divide through by cos t so sin/cos collapses to tan; simplification of a given relation via the quotient relation rather than reading a table (LO-2) or building a triangle (C-6.1-LO-1)
cos A = 4/5 is a 3-4-5 triangle, not a standard angle; the third side comes from Pythagoras and tan A is read off the sides - the defining-from-sides outcome
cosec(75+t) and sec(15-t) are complementary, as are cot(35-t) and tan(55+t); the entire expression cancels on the complementary rewrite and no identity or table value is touched

two equally weighted steps: cos 9a = sin a is solved by the complementary relation to get a = 9, then tan 45 = 1 is a table lookup. Unlike sha fd4c74e7 the answer is a standard-angle value, so both codes earn their place

inverse table lookup twice (sin a = 1/2 gives 30, cos b = 1/2 gives 60); the complementary fact that they sum to 90 is the answer, not the method, so not C-6.3-LO-1
homogeneous ratio in sin and cos: divide numerator and denominator by cos t to express everything in tan t. tan t = 3/4 is not a standard angle, so LO-2 and never C-6.1-LO-2
parametric elimination of theta using sec^2 - tan^2 = 1; the identity is the tool for proving a relation between x, y, p, q - the LO-2 use, not the LO-1 derivation
literal twin of sha 29a4a16c with a and b for 4 and 1; same divide-by-cos technique, so the same outcome is the honest answer rather than an invented distinction
